questions.question: Product [X] formed in the above reaction is:
questions.explanation:
The reaction proceeds in three steps:

Step 1: The hydroxyl group of butan-2-ol is replaced by iodine using NaI and H3PO4. This is a nucleophilic substitution reaction.

Step 2: The resulting 2-iodobutane reacts with magnesium in dry ether to form a Grignard reagent, sec-butylmagnesium iodide.

Step 3: The Grignard reagent is a strong base and reacts with heavy water (D2O), an acid, to form 2-deuterobutane.

questions.question: 29. The product of the following reaction is P. The number of hydroxyl groups present in the product P is __________.
questions.explanation:
In the given reaction, 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde has an acidic proton on its hydroxyl group. Phenylmagnesium bromide (PhMgBr) is a strong base. The acid-base reaction between the acidic proton and the Grignard reagent is much faster than the nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl group of the aldehyde.

Since only one equivalent of PhMgBr is used, it will be consumed in the acid-base reaction, forming Benzene as the major product.

So the total number of hydroxyl group present in major product will be zero.

questions.question: Grignard reagent RMgBr(P) reacts with water and forms a gas (Q). One gram of Q occupies $1.4 \text{ dm}^3$ at STP. (P) on reaction with dry ice in dry ether followed by $H_{3}O^{+}$ forms a compound (Z). 0.1 mole of (Z) will weigh ________ g. (Nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Given that 1 gram of gas Q occupies \(1.4 \text{ dm}^3\) (which is 1.4 L) at STP.

We know that 1 mole of any gas at STP occupies 22.4 L. We can calculate the molar mass of gas Q.

$$
\text{Molar mass of Q} = \frac{\text{Mass of Q}}{\text{Volume of Q at STP}} \times 22.4 \text{ L/mol}
$$

$$
\text{Molar mass of Q} = \frac{1 \text{ g}}{1.4 \text{ L}} \times 22.4 \text{ L/mol} = 16 \text{ g/mol}
$$

A gas with a molar mass of 16 g/mol is methane (\(CH_{4}\)). So, Q is \(CH_{4}\).

Grignard reagents (RMgBr) react with water to produce an alkane (RH). Since the gas formed (Q) is methane (\(CH_{4}\)), the alkyl group R in the Grignard reagent must be a methyl group (\(CH_{3}\)).

Therefore, the Grignard reagent (P) is methylmagnesium bromide (\(CH_{3}MgBr\)).

The Grignard reagent (P) then reacts with dry ice (solid \(CO_{2}\)) followed by acidic hydrolysis (\(H_{3}O^{+}\)) to form a carboxylic acid (Z). This is a standard reaction for preparing carboxylic acids from Grignard reagents.

The compound (Z) is acetic acid (\(CH_{3}COOH\)).

The molar mass of acetic acid (\(CH_{3}COOH\)) is \(12.01 + 3(1.01) + 12.01 + 2(16.00) + 1.01 \approx 60 \text{ g/mol}\).

Finally, we need to find the weight of 0.1 mole of (Z).

$$
\text{Weight} = \text{moles} \times \text{Molar mass} = 0.1 \text{ mol} \times 60 \text{ g/mol} = 6 \text{ g}
$$

questions.question: An atomic substance A of molar mass 12 g $mol^{-1}$ has a cubic crystal structure with edge length of 300 pm. The no. of atoms present in one unit cell of A is $\underline{\hspace{2cm}}$ (Nearest integer) Given the density of A is 3.0 g $mL^{-1}$ and $N_{A}$ = 6.02$\times$10$^{23} mol^{-1}$
questions.explanation:
Given:

• Molar mass (M) = 12 g \(mol^{-1}\)
• Edge length (a) = 300 pm = 300 \(\times\) \(10^{-12}\) m = 300 \(\times\) \(10^{-10}\) cm
• Density (d) = 3.0 g \(mL^{-1}\) = 3.0 g \(cm^{-3}\)
• Avogadro's number (\(N_{A}\)) = 6.02 \(\times\) \(10^{23}\) \(mol^{-1}\)

$$
d = \frac{Z \times M}{N_A \times a^3}
$$

Where Z is the number of atoms per unit cell.

$$
3 = \frac{Z \times 12}{6.02 \times 10^{23} \times (300 \times 10^{-10})^3}
$$

$$
Z = \frac{3 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} \times (300 \times 10^{-10})^3}{12}
$$

$$
Z = \frac{3 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} \times (3 \times 10^{-8})^3}{12}
$$

$$
Z = \frac{3 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} \times 27 \times 10^{-24}}{12}
$$

$$
Z = \frac{3 \times 6.02 \times 27 \times 10^{-1}}{12}
$$

$$
Z = \frac{487.62 \times 10^{-1}}{12}
$$

$$
Z = 40.635 \times 10^{-1}
$$

$$
Z = 4.0635
$$

Since Z must be an integer, rounding 4.0635 to the nearest integer gives 4.

questions.question: The maximum number of RBr producing 2-methylbutane by above sequence of reactions is _____. (Consider the structural isomers only)
questions.explanation:
The reaction sequence involves the formation of a Grignard reagent (RMgBr) from RBr, followed by hydrolysis to yield an alkane (RH). In this case, the product is 2-methylbutane.

To produce 2-methylbutane, the R group in RBr must be a 2-methylbutyl group. We need to find all possible structural isomers of RBr with this carbon skeleton.

Total number of possible structural RBr = 4
